title: fix: refresh prepared PRs from the live target branch
body: Closes #190561. ## What Problem This Solves A conversation continuing an existing PR can report that its base is current even after the target branch advances. GitHub PR details may retain an older base SHA while the branch-ref endpoint already names the new tip. Using that PR-detail SHA leaves newer target files out of the workspace. After integrating a newer base, repeated preparation must also avoid resetting the review comparison to that older metadata. ## User Impact A fresh `refresh_base` integrates the current tip of the verified target repository and branch for both imported PRs and PRs originally published by the conversation. Repeating `prepare_pr` afterward preserves the correct review comparison, so integrated upstream files do not appear as PR changes merely because GitHub's PR details lag. The accepted PR head and identity remain intact for subsequent publication. A pending conflict continues against its accepted commit; a later fresh refresh picks up further target changes. There are no configuration, schema, dependency, or permission changes. ## Why This Change Was Made The preparation owner already verifies the PR destination and distinguishes new selection from pending integration. It now uses the existing guarded branch-ref reader for a fresh refresh, and when preparation sees disagreement between the accepted base and the metadata for the same destination. Reading the live ref distinguishes stale metadata from a target that actually moved, without adding a cache or another integration mechanism. The registered-action regression keeps PR metadata unchanged while the same Git branch advances, then repeats preparation and checks the saved comparison and cached diff. The existing conflict/publication scenario advances the target during a pending conflict and verifies that resolution finishes the earlier target before a fresh refresh imports the new tip. An existing preparation fixture now creates the actual branch it retargets to. The 50-line test-budget allocation covers those missing conditions and that required fixture adaptation. ## Evidence On unchanged main, both PR-origin variants returned `current` with the old commit instead of the independently advanced branch commit. A follow-on regression also reproduced the stale review comparison after repeated preparation. The corrected candidate passes all 85 cases across the five related action, preparation, source-adoption, and integration files. Changed-file formatting/lint and affected production/test type checks passed; unaffected type-graph results were retained under unchanged consumer contracts. The five test files passed with one worker in 228.05 seconds (230.72 seconds including the native shard wrapper). They use real Git, request authority, and workspace state with external GitHub fixtures; helper-only tests would miss the selection and recovery boundaries. Hosted CI timing for this revision remains pending. The live baseline reproduced the stale result through actual guest conversations for both PR origins, with independent GitHub PR-detail and branch-ref reads. On the corrected build, both conversations selected the live target, retained the accepted base while it advanced during conflict resolution, then picked up the newer tip on a fresh refresh. Both published directly to their original PRs without intervening preparation; original head history, saved files, authors and public metadata were preserved. All selected CI jobs and both source reviews are green for the current head. After publication refreshed GitHub’s metadata, a further real target-branch advance restored the stale-metadata condition. Both guest conversations refreshed that target and repeated preparation while preserving the correct review base, files, indexes, heads and bindings. Returning guests remained denied merge after admin inspection; authorized admins then merged the original fixture PRs, with independently verified file trees matching their final published heads. The matched captures and recording below show the initial fresh-base transition; separate native receipts establish the later resolution, publication, repeated-preparation and permission checks. This is isolated Guest Lab proof, not a production deployment or full release claim. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Session\-published PR | ![Session\-published PR: old base reported current while the target file is absent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c72dcb04-ad79-4577-a679-38e4d3560856) | ![Session\-published PR: live base selected with conflicts and the target file present](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7eb63f5-2f3b-4535-8480-aad1469fa0d5) | | Imported PR | ![Imported PR: old base reported current while the target file is absent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f16acac-2303-4e85-a10a-dd885e3028b3) | ![Imported PR: live base selected with conflicts and the target file present](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b46a84ef-666e-46cc-aa2d-ac7f874054a9) | ### Guest refresh selects the live base and returns actual conflicts https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d8caf0b-4101-4d25-9440-2b9f34022a7f ### Visual verification - Baseline: d797c14276f3327227e13556557cc58f88db9c71 \(native carrier 681513d48b3bbc42764d81bfbcdf241e64229122\) - Exact head: `a3a00c492bb36c4790169facd3c6549c8cd06815` - Scenario: Advance the existing PR target branch without changing its name while PR details retain the older base SHA, then ask the guest to refresh its saved work\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.9\-32892a4877a6\-2026\-11\-01T18\-25\-47\.179Z; native carrier tree 0fbe50b178c2370fbfdd23a955847ec328f15d81 equals the reviewed head tree\. - Before: current at old PR metadata fe892761; base\-policy\.txt absent - After: conflicts at live branch 0b8d8025; base\-policy\.txt present - Saved work: Priority/express delivery and unpublished tracking note preserved - Both PR origins exercised through actual guest conversations and independent GitHub PR\-detail/ref reads\. - The target branch names and original PR identities stay unchanged\. - Matched 780×662 crops, dark theme, and the same fixture conversations; baseline is the retained older runtime, not a claim of whole\-runtime parity\. - Original build metadata is preserved; the candidate native carrier has the exact reviewed source tree\. - All decoded frames and matched stills were inspected\. Original frame timing is retained; initial scale normalization and short endpoint holds are disclosed\. No real\-time playback or product\-latency claim\. - The recording ends at fresh\-base conflicts\. Subsequent pinning, resolution, publication and repeated preparation use separate native receipts\.
